review.why: Teaches how to write and test agent skills by treating them like code: baseline failures with subagents, write the skill, close loopholes, verify.
review.summary: Maps test-driven development onto skill writing: run a pressure scenario without the skill, record the rationalizations, write a minimal skill that addresses them, verify compliance and refactor. It defines what a skill is and is not, when to create one, skill types and points to guidance on discovery, flowcharts, persuasion principles and testing with subagents.
strengths: Insists on watching an agent fail without the skill first
Clear when not to write a skill
Includes official authoring guidance as a reference
cautions: Requires understanding the companion test-driven skill
Testing with subagents costs time and tokens
Nine reference files and a rendering script are not read here
